question: Albert Einstein was awarded the Nobel Prize for ______ in 1921.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Photoelectric Effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Albert Einstein **was given the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921** "for his services to theoretical physics, particularly for his discovery of the **photoelectric effect law**."
 
• One year later, in 1922, Albert Einstein was awarded the Nobel Prize.
 
• **The Nobel Committee for Physics** ruled during the 1921 selection process that none of the nominees satisfied the requirements set in Alfred Nobel's bequest.
 
• The Nobel Prize can be reserved until the next year, according to the Nobel Foundation's regulations, and this statute was followed.
 
• As a result, Albert Einstein was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in **1922**, a year after winning the prize in 1921.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• When **electromagnetic radiation, **such as light, strikes a substance, electrons are emitted. Photoelectrons are electrons that are emitted in this manner. 
 
• The process through which an unstable atomic nucleus loses energy by radiation is known as **radioactive decay**.
 
• **The Doppler effect** is defined as a change in frequency of a wave as a result of a moving observer relative to the wave source.
 
• **The theory of relativity **usually refers to two connected ideas devised and published by Albert Einstein in 1905 and 1915, respectively: special relativity and general relativity. In the absence of gravity, special relativity applies to all physical events.
